computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied to Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si ANT750 specimen using measured microstructure (ferrite/bainite fractions and grain sizes, GND density, Taylor factor)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Input features: σ0, σg, σd, σOrowan contributions; output: YS. GA search over six hyper-parameters (n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_split, etc.); population size 30, crossover probability 0.7, mutation probability 0.3, 30 generations (converges after 26th). Optimized hyper-parameters: n_estimators=1657, max_depth=51, min_samples_split=3, min_samples_leaf=1.0, max_features=0.85, max_samples=0.92.

computational_details.simulation_method: Machine-learning yield-strength prediction (Genetic-Algorithm-optimized Extremely Randomized Trees, GA-Extra Trees)

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For ANT750 (750 °C): measured YS = 709 MPa; GA-Extra Trees predicted 721 MPa (difference 12 MPa) vs plain Extra Trees 743 MPa (difference 34 MPa); overall average error for the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloys annealed at 750–850 °C was 1.56 %.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Experimental steel with composition (mass fraction) Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si melted in a vacuum induction furnace.
After melting, the ingot was hot forged.
Specimens heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min prior to hot rolling.
Six-pass rolling on a φ350 mm×350 mm high-stiffness two-high hot rolling mill; initial rolling temperature 1100 °C, final rolling temperature 880 °C, cumulative reduction ratio 90 %.
Cold rolling experiment with a total reduction ratio of 60 % performed on a four-high reversible cold rolling mill.
Cold-rolled specimens annealed at 750 °C for 30 min followed by air cooling to room temperature; this is the step that distinguishes ANT750 from ANT800/ANT850.
After annealing and air cooling, specimens were held at 400 °C for 30 min and air-cooled, yielding the ANT750 group.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests on an Instron 3382 universal electronic materials testing machine; three samples tested per group; specimens air-cooled after 750 °C/30 min annealing + 400 °C/30 min.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex ferrite + bainite microstructure with retained austenite content <5% (its strengthening contribution neglected); Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation so no significant precipitates form.

unmapped_findings: The tabulated measured yield strength of AN750 is 709 MPa (Table 3), yet the engineering stress–strain curve for the 750 °C condition (Fig. 12, black) exhibits a long plateau slightly above 1000 MPa from ~13 % to 30 % strain ending near 33 % strain — the high plateau is the flow/UTS level while the reported YS (0.2 % offset-type value) is 709 MPa.

The Orowan strengthening contribution of the Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si test steel is 0 MPa because Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitates form and no precipitation strengthening occurs.
Retained austenite content in the ANT750 specimen is <5 % and its strengthening contribution was therefore neglected.
Average error between predicted and measured YS for the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloys annealed at 750–850 °C was 1.56 % (the 750 °C ANT750 case contributes to this average).

SHAP/feature-importance analysis (Fig. 17, performed for the Fe-9.7Mn-2.04Al-0.99Si-0.52V-0.42C composition, not ANT750) ranked dislocation strengthening as the dominant contributor, followed by Orowan strengthening, then fine-grain and solid-solution strengthening.
